title: Nile cruises, explained before you sail
standfirst: A Nile cruise can mean a sailing boat with eight guests or a ship with a hundred and forty. We explain how the vessels differ, what the price pays for and what a week on the river is really like, then show you cruises you can book.

sections.heading: Three ways to sail the Nile
paragraphs: Most Nile cruises sail between Luxor and Aswan, past the same temples. What changes is the boat. A dahabiya is a sailing houseboat with a handful of cabins that moors at quiet riverbanks. A motor cruise ship carries many more guests, has a pool on the sun deck and keeps to a set timetable. A few historic paddle steamers sit in between.
Choose the vessel first and the rest follows: how many people you share the trip with, where you moor at night and how free the days are.

sections.heading: Why one five-star cabin costs ten times another
paragraphs: “Five-star” on the Nile is not a single standard. The price follows the size of the boat, the number of crew per guest, the cabin, the season and what is included. We break each price into those parts so you can see what you are paying for.
Crew gratuities are always separate and paid on board, and a cruise runs from check-in to check-out: flights, transfers and extra tours are added only if you choose them.

sections.heading: How Nilecruz works
paragraphs: Independent operators supply the vessels, cabins and prices. We publish our own evaluation of each vessel, scored out of 100 against the same seven criteria, and show reviews from other sites separately with their source.
When you book, Nilecruz makes the booking and takes your payment as the operator’s booking agent. You see one honest starting price before you sign in, and every cabin and date after.

faqs.q: When is the Nile cruise season?
faqs.a: Most cruises sail all year. October to April is cooler and busier; May to September is hot, quieter and often cheaper. Departures and prices for each vessel show on its page.

faqs.q: Do I need to book flights and transfers separately?
faqs.a: Yes. A cruise runs from check-in on the first day to check-out on the last. Flights, airport transfers and extra tours are separate, and you add only what you need.
